item.title: This Al Mahra Residence Is a Contemporary Expression of Place
item.description: Through raw yet refined materials and a radically open plan, Marie Claire Mrad crafts an interior architecture that responds to light, climate, and the rhythms of daily life.

item.title: Etereo and StudioTwentySeven Present the Mo.du.lo Collection
item.description: The Mo.du.lo Collection from Etereo and StudioTwentySeven features thick blocks of green glass, offering a unique depth and transparency.

item.title: Umami Brings Depth + Harmony to Alabaster Lighting
item.description: Designed by Alain Ellouz and Ana Moussinet, the Umami lighting collection is grounded in the Japanese concept of nature at its peak.

item.title: Il Bronzetto’s EDGE Door Handle Holds Court
item.description: Designed by OmniDe and handcrafted in Italy, the EDGE door handle blends architectural geometry, ergonomic precision, and multi-finish versatility.

item.title: The Art of What We Throw Away
item.description: Rhea Gupte’s COMPOST finds color, texture, and meaning in frozen food scraps – transforming everyday waste into art, ritual, and shared experience.

item.title: Dyson’s New HushJet Compact Purifier is Small but Mighty
item.description: Able to efficiently filter air through an entire room with close to no noise, the new device is inconspicuous in size yet powerful.

item.title: Dig in to Momos by José A. Gandía-Blasco for GAN
item.description: Evoking the warmth and texture of handmade dumplings, the MOMOS Collection by José A. Gandía-Blasco for GAN comes in two delectable colors.

item.title: The Scale Collective Brings Tactile Warmth to This Beverly Hills Penthouse
item.description: High above Los Angeles Country Club, Sara Alexander inverts the luxury penthouse formula with absorptive fibers and sculptural curves.

item.title: Charlotte Chesnais + Maison Christofle Present Carrousel Flatware
item.description: Take a trip every time you set the table with the Carrousel Flatware collection by Charlotte Chesnais and Maison Christofle.

item.title: A Form of Hug: The Mysa Chair by Studio Kohlhass
item.description: A hug requires that we lean on one another, oxytocin delivered directly to the brain. The power of this simple gesture is sometimes understated—elegant in its simplicity, tender in its sweetness.
